subject: gk
question: Which of the following earthquake waves is more destructive?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Surface waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Surface waves are seismic waves that travel along the Earth's surface and are typically the most destructive type of seismic wave during an earthquake.
 
• They have larger amplitudes and longer durations compared to body waves, leading to more significant ground movement.
 
• Surface waves are divided into two main types: Love waves and Rayleigh waves.
 
• Love waves cause horizontal shifting of the ground, while Rayleigh waves cause a rolling motion, similar to ocean waves.
 
• Because of their higher amplitude and lower frequency, surface waves cause more damage to buildings and infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Body Waves**

 
 
• These are seismic waves that travel through the Earth's interior.
 
• They are divided into Primary (P) waves and Secondary (S) waves.
 
• P-waves are compressional waves that travel fastest and can move through both solid and liquid layers of the Earth.
 
• S-waves are shear waves that travel slower than P-waves and can only move through solid materials.
 
 
 
• **Primary Waves (P-Waves)**
 
 
• P-waves are the first waves to be detected by seismographs during an earthquake.
 
• They cause particles in the ground to compress and expand in the direction of wave propagation.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Waves (S-Waves)**
 
 
• S-waves are slower than P-waves and arrive after them.
 
• They cause particles in the ground to move perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation, resulting in a shearing motion.
 
 
 
• **Seismograph**
 
 
• A seismograph is an instrument used to detect and record earthquakes.
 
• It measures the motion of the ground and helps in determining the location and magnitude of an earthquake.
